_meta.indication: LUMIZYME (alglucosidase alfa) is a lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme indicated for patients 8 years and older with late (non-infantile) onset Pompe disease (GAA deficiency) who do not have evidence of cardiac hypertrophy.
_meta.receipt_date: May 30, 2008 (original BLA); current complete response submission December 16, 2009

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 2:1 to 20 mg/kg alglucosidase alfa IV every two weeks or placebo for 78 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 8 years and older with late-onset Pompe disease, naïve to enzyme replacement therapy, ambulatory, not requiring invasive ventilatory support, with FVC between 30 and 79% of predicted.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: distance walked during the six-minute walk test (6MWT) and upright percent predicted forced vital capacity (FVC); the statistical plan stated the 6MWT was to be examined first and FVC evaluated only if the 6MWT effect was statistically significant.
pivotal_trials.result: 6MWT (ANCOVA) difference between arms was not statistically significant, p=0.06 (p shifted from 0.035 to 0.06 with re-randomization testing). FVC mean change from baseline difference 3.40% predicted (95% CI 1.03, 5.77).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were infusion reactions including anaphylaxis, urticaria, diarrhea, vomiting, dyspnea, pruritus, rash/erythema. Serious reactions included anaphylaxis; two LUMIZYME-treated patients discontinued due to anaphylactic reactions. Based on exposure of 90 patients.
target_moa: Alglucosidase alfa is a recombinant human acid α-glucosidase (GAA) that replaces deficient lysosomal enzyme; after IV administration it is internalized via cell membrane mannose-6-phosphate receptors and taken up by lysosomes, where it degrades glycogen by catalyzing the hydrolysis of its glycosidic linkages in Pompe disease.
modality: enzyme (recombinant human acid α-glucosidase, enzyme replacement therapy)

boxed_warning.content: Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions, severe allergic reactions and immune mediated reactions have been observed during LUMIZYME infusions; appropriate medical support should be available. Because of the potential risk of rapid disease progression in Pompe disease patients less than 8 years of age, LUMIZYME is available only through a restricted distribution program (LUMIZYME ACE Program).

rems.type: A REMS was required to mitigate the risk of rapid disease progression in infantile-onset and late-onset patients under 8 years of age and the risks of anaphylaxis and severe allergic reactions; the REMS consists of a communication plan, elements to assure safe use, an implementation system, and a timetable for assessments.

advisory_committee.vote: The Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) met October 21, 2008 and voted 16-1 that effectiveness of the 2000 L product had been demonstrated in LOTS; twelve members recommended accelerated approval under Subpart E based on the FVC endpoint.

description.text: Expanded indication to all patients with Pompe disease including infantile-onset and late-onset patients less than 8 years of age, and eliminated the Lumizyme REMS requirement

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application proposes to revise the indication for Lumizyme to extend the population to all patients with Pompe disease (acid \alpha-glucosidase (GAA) deficiency), including infantile-onset and late-onset patients less than 8 years of age.

orphan_indication.text: Alglucosidase alfa was designated Orphan Status in 1997; this biological product for this indication received orphan drug designation.

citations.quote: Aglucosidase alfa was designated Orphan Status in 1997. PREA does not apply to products with Orphan Status.
Because this biological product for this indication has received orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

basis.text: The original BLA (Lumizyme 2000 L) was granted a priority review.

citations.quote: The BLA was granted a priority review and was discussed at a closed and an open session of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on October 21, 2008.

summary.text: The original BLA for Lumizyme 2000 L (submitted May 30, 2008) was granted priority review and taken to the EMDAC on October 21, 2008, where the committee voted 16-1 that effectiveness was demonstrated and recommended accelerated approval based on FVC. After multiple Complete Response actions (first CR dated February 27, 2009) for manufacturing/CMC deficiencies, FDA and the applicant agreed that Pompe Registry outcomes data could support regular (not accelerated) approval. Alglucosidase alfa carries orphan drug designation (1997). The product was approved May 24, 2010 with a Boxed Warning and a REMS.

citations.quote: The BLA was granted a priority review and was discussed at a closed and an open session of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on October 21, 2008.

This BLA application was presented to Endocrinology and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on October 21, 2008. Although the Committee voted 16-1 that the effectiveness of the 2000 L product had been demonstrated in LOTS, twelve Committee members recommended that the product should be granted accelerated approval under Subpart E, based on the data for the endpoint FVC, an endpoint considered to be a surrogate

came to an agreement that additional clinical information (i.e. outcomes data) from the Pompe Registry, (a multinational disease registry established in response to a post-marketing commitment that was a condition for the 2006 approval of Myozyme), may provide sufficient clinical outcome information to support regular approval for the 2000 L product, instead of approval under Subpart E.
Aglucosidase alfa was designated Orphan Status in 1997. PREA does not apply to products with Orphan Status.

requirement.text: A retrospective immunogenicity study based on the pattern of antibody responses that may predict development of anaphylaxis, allergic reactions, and immune-complex mediated reactions in patients enrolled in LOTS and LOTS Extension Studies.

citations.quote: 1. A retrospective immunogenicity study based on the pattern of antibody responses that may predict the development of anaphylaxis, allergic reactions, and immune-complex mediated reactions in patients enrolled in the Late Onset Treatment Study (LOTS) and LOTS Extension Studies.

requirement.text: A prospective safety study conducted within the ongoing Pompe Registry to assess the known serious risks of anaphylaxis and severe allergic reactions, and signals of severe cutaneous and systemic immune complex-mediated reactions with LUMIZYME.

citations.quote: 2. A prospective safety study conducted within the ongoing Pompe Registry to assess the known serious risks of anaphylaxis and severe allergic reactions, and signals of severe cutaneous and systemic immune complex-mediated reactions with Lumizyme (alglucosidase alfa) treatment.

requirement.text: A retrospective study of patients in LOTS and LOTS Extension Studies whose efficacy responses (6MWT and/or % predicted FVC) appeared affected by the pattern of their antibody response.

citations.quote: 3. A retrospective study of patients enrolled in the LOTS and LOTS Extension Studies whose efficacy responses (i.e., high performance or poor performance) as assessed by the 6 minute walk test (6MWT) and/or % predicted forced vital capacity (FVC) appeared to have been affected by the pattern of their antibody response.

requirement.text: A long-term follow-up study to evaluate long-term efficacy and immunogenicity outcomes in a subpopulation of LOTS and LOTS Extension patients with substantial improvement in 6MWT, conducted as a sub-study within the ongoing Pompe Registry.

citations.quote: 4. A long-term follow-up study to evaluate long-term efficacy and immunogenicity outcomes in a subpopulation of patients in LOTS and LOTS Extension Studies whose response to Lumizyme (alglucosidase alfa) is associated with substantial improvement over baseline in the 6 minute walk test (6MWT) results. This study will be conducted as a sub-study within the ongoing Pompe Registry.

requirement.text: Prospective outcome data collected within the ongoing Pompe Registry to assess the long-term efficacy of LUMIZYME.

citations.quote: 5. As part of the ongoing Pompe Registry, prospective outcome data will be collected in patients enrolled in the Registry to assess the long-term efficacy of Lumizyme (alglucosidase alfa).

requirement.text: A prospective pharmacokinetic study within the ongoing Pompe Registry to characterize the pharmacokinetics of LUMIZYME in pediatric patients aged 8 to 18 years.

citations.quote: 6. A prospective pharmacokinetic (PK) study conducted within the ongoing Pompe Registry study to characterize the pharmacokinetics of Lumizyme (alglucosidase alfa) in pediatric patients in the age range of 8 years to 18 years.

date.text: Prior Complete Response letter dated February 27, 2009 (initial CR action)

basis.text: Could not approve in the first cycle because of serious manufacturing deficiencies at the Allston Landing, MA facility and CMC deficiencies in the BLA, plus lack of agreement on the post-approval study design and REMS.

citations.quote: The Agency was unable to approve the product in the first cycle because of serious manufacturing deficiencies identified in the inspection of the Allston Landing, MA manufacturing facility and CMC deficiencies in the BLA.
